item.title: Finite-size geometric crossover toward fragmentation of the potential energy shell in the quantum random energy model
item.description: arXiv:2610.21631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum random energy model (QREM) is a paradigmatic model for studying delocalization-localization transitions at finite energy density in Fock space. In the computational basis, its diagonal energies are independent Gaussian random variables, in contrast to the correlated energies of local interacting models such as the disordered XXZ chain. In this work, we construct a potential energy shell associated with a basis state, defined through its energy variance, and investigate its connectivity on the Fock-space hypercube. As the transverse field is varied, this energy-selected subgraph undergoes a finite-size geometric crossover between fully connected and fragmented regimes. Furthermore, we observe a correlation between the shell connectivity and the finite-size fractal dimension of the eigenstates, as extracted from the participation entropy. For the QREM, the statistical independence of the diagonal energies allows the shell connectivity to be analyzed as an effective independent site percolation problem on the hypercube, with its crossover scale estimated within a one-hop approximation. At finite energy density, this estimate gives a nonmonotonic dependence of the crossover scale on system size $L$: increasing $L$ initially favors connectivity, while beyond an energy-dependent scale $L^*(\varepsilon)$ the trend reverses towards fragmentation.
item.dc:creator: Ishita Modak, Vatsana Tiwari, Soumya Bera

item.title: Attention over noisy examples: generalization and memorization in the exponential Hopfield network
item.description: arXiv:2610.22191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Hebbian learning from examples a Hopfield network of $N$ neurons is not supplied with the $K$ archetypes it has to retrieve but with $M$ blurred examples of each, of quality $r$, and whether it can infer them depends on the load $\alpha=K/N$ (interference among them) and on the dataset entropy $\rho=(1-r^2)/(Mr^2)$ (how little the examples say about them). We transfer this protocol to the exponential Hopfield model, whose zero-temperature update is a step of softmax attention with the unlabelled examples as keys. A signal-to-noise analysis gives in closed form the overlap between the output and an unseen archetype, $m^{(1)}={\rm erf}(1/\sqrt{2\rho_{\rm eff}})$: the majority-rule law of the pairwise model at small load, with $\rho$ replaced by an attention entropy $\rho_{\rm eff}$ built from the weight the softmax gives to the correct class and the number of examples it spreads it over. Two consequences follow. First, in a window of inverse temperatures $\beta$ that widens as $\sqrt N$ the interference between archetypes is exponentially small in $N\beta$: the load drops out and the number of archetypes that can be learnt grows as $\exp(c\sqrt N)$. Second, learning fails differently: in the pairwise model through a spin-glass phase, in the exponential model through memorization: the softmax concentrates its weight on the training example closest to the input and returns it in place of the archetype. Seen from the input the softmax weights are those of the random energy model, and memorization is its freezing transition, at $\beta\sqrt{N(1-r^2)}\simeq\sqrt{2\ln M}$; it is measurable on a head whose keys are examples as the number of examples carrying weight. On MNIST the diagnostic follows the random-energy prediction; on fashion-MNIST it detects sub-clusters in the classes, and the best accuracy lies beyond the memorization threshold, where the softmax reads out a local sub-prototype.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Alemanno

item.title: Information-Theoretic Limits for Rectangular Spiked Matrix Models with Rotationally Invariant Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.16797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the information-theoretic limits of inference in rectangular rank-one spiked matrix models with additive rotationally invariant noise, thereby going beyond the standard assumption of independent noise entries. Using the replica method from statistical physics, we derive a variational formula for the mutual information between the signal and the data, together with a system of saddle point equations predicting the minimum mean squared error in estimating the rank-one spike. We further show that, in the Bayes-optimal setting, these saddle point equations coincide with the fixed point equations of the state evolution of a recently proposed orthogonal approximate message passing algorithm with Bayes-optimal denoisers. This equivalence provides an algorithmic interpretation of the replica prediction and supports the Bayes-optimality of orthogonal approximate message passing whenever the relevant fixed point is unique. Numerical evaluations of the saddle point equations for several rotationally invariant noise ensembles and signal priors, together with finite-size simulations of the algorithm, confirm the asymptotic predictions. They illustrate both regimes with a unique informative fixed point, where orthogonal approximate message passing is predicted to attain the minimum mean squared error, and regimes with multiple fixed points, where a statistical-to-computational gap exists.
item.dc:creator: Qun Chen, Rudy Skerk, Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Junjie Ma, Haochuan Zhang

item.title: Transport in multilayer graphene: resistance from stacking faults
item.description: arXiv:2610.20713v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multilayer graphene exhibits rich possibilities for stacking. While natural bulk graphite predominantly occurs in the Bernal structure, where layers are stacked in an $-ABAB-$ pattern, rhombohedral stacking has sprung to prominence recently. It is well known that Bernal graphite exhibits anisotropic transport, with high resistance to currents along the stacking axis. Careful experiments using pillar geometries have measured out-of-plane resistance, attributing it to stacking faults where planes slip out of the nominal $ABAB$ sequence. The observed resistance shows anomalously large, non-Gaussian, sample-to-sample variations. In this article, we build a theoretical framework to calculate $c$-axis resistance of graphene stacks with an arbitrary stacking arrangement. Our approach builds on the idea that, regardless of stacking sequence, we have in-plane translational symmetry. With in-plane momentum as a good quantum number, $c$-axis transport reduces to an effectively one-dimensional problem that can be addressed using the Landauer paradigm. We calculate the resistances of a variety of simple stacking faults in both Bernal and rhombohedral systems. We also calculate the resistance of a rhombohedral 'slab' embedded between Bernal leads. Remarkably, despite both Bernal and rhombohedral graphite being metallic, the system exhibits insulating behaviour. We attribute this to Fermi surface mismatch. We next calculate the resistance of a multilayer sample with stacking disorder. Resistance is non-self-averaging, akin to a one-dimensional wire where disorder has a strong localizing effect. The median resistance grows exponentially with stack size, indicating insulating character driven by localization. Our results demonstrate that transport measurements on mesoscopic graphitic pillars serve as signatures of stacking faults, and in particular, probe localization-driven physics.
item.dc:creator: C. M. Wilson, R. Ganesh, K. V. Samokhin

item.title: Quantum oscillations in a solvable model of a Kondo insulator
item.description: arXiv:2610.20734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the effects of interactions on the low-energy density of states (SdH) and magnetization (dHvA) quantum oscillations (QOs) in a Kondo insulator. Toward this end we introduce a generalization of the periodic Anderson model with Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) interactions at each site that is exactly solvable in the large-$N$ limit, where $N$ is the number of flavors of the heavy $f$ electrons. We show analytically and numerically that the insulating state remains stable in terms of spectrum, thermodynamics, and transport at low temperatures even for interaction strengths much larger than non-interacting band gap of the hybridization-gap insulator. We analytically derive generalizations of Lifshitz-Kosevich (LK) formulae, distinct for the SdH and dHvA QOs, for the interacting insulator. We find that the SdH oscillation frequencies, $F_0\pm \delta F$, corresponding to the conduction and valence band edges, can be weakly renormalized by interaction relative to their non-interacting values. In contrast, dHvA QO frequency $F_0$ is not renormalized by interactions, and remains the same as that for the non-interacting unhybridized bands. The QO amplitudes show a remarkable difference: the dHvA amplitude is essentially unaffected by interactions, while the SdH amplitude is strongly enhanced due to gap renormalization.
item.dc:creator: Abhisek Samanta, Mohit Randeria, Sumilan Banerjee

item.title: The Blume-Capel Model as a $\phi^6$ Field Theory: A Monte Carlo and Flow Model Study
item.description: arXiv:2610.20982v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report Monte Carlo simulations of a continuous spin variant of the Blume-Capel model. We compute the phase diagrams in the crystal-field-temperature plane, as a function of the softness of the spins. We show that normalizing flows, a class of generative models capable of direct sampling without autocorrelation, are effective samplers across the phase diagram, including in the first-order transition region and in the vicinity of the tricritical point. Finite-size scaling analyses of flow samples locate the first- and second-order transitions as well as the tricritical point with accuracy comparable to canonical and extended-ensemble Monte Carlo.
item.dc:creator: Ejaaz Merali, Ryan Larson, Ehsan Khatami, Richard T. Scalettar

item.title: Partial Localization and Multifractality in Heterogeneous Population Growth with Resetting
item.description: arXiv:2610.22038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a model of heterogeneous multiplicative growth with mean-field redistribution and independent local stochastic resetting. The model describes populations or wealth distributed over sites with quenched growth-rate heterogeneity, while resets represent random local extinction or bankruptcy events. At large redistribution or resetting rate, we find a delocalized phase and we compute the growth rate as well as the stationary distribution of the population of a given site. We show that reset-free growth episodes generate power-law stationary tails with site-dependent exponents. For weak resetting and redistribution, favorable sites can undergo long reset-free episodes and localize. This produces a partially localized phase, in which a finite fraction of the total population is carried by a small set of sites whose identity changes on an $O(1)$ time scale within a subextensive pool of $N^{u^\star}$ favorable candidates, with $0<u^\star<1$. We derive the corresponding growth rate from a saddle point analysis, and show that the averaged stationary fractions display multifractal behavior.
item.dc:creator: Maximilien Bernard, Giuseppe Del Vecchio Del Vecchio, Jean-Philippe Bouchaud, Pierre Le Doussal

item.title: Spontaneous and Collective Learning in a Minimal Agent-Environment Model
item.description: arXiv:2509.23212v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: How can information be extracted from data without explicit guidance or rewards? We investigate this question in a minimal setting where a classifying agent is exposed to a stream of structured data produced by a generative environment, and evolves by seeking consistency of its own labels in time. We find that imposing a simplicity bias on the classification rule can drive the dynamics toward label-coherent steady states, which we coin functional replicators. Remarkably, these persistent labeling rules align with the latent structure of the data. Using analytical tools from statistical mechanics, we characterize this spontaneous learning phase transition. Extending the analysis to a collective of agents that pool labels from one another, we show that interaction reshapes the learning phase boundary, in some regimes enabling spontaneous learning that no isolated agent can achieve, while suppressing it in others. Our minimal framework thus opens a route to decentralized learning through label exchange alone, requiring no access to the internal weights of other agents.
item.dc:creator: Sebastiano Ariosto, Jerome Garnier-Brun, Luca Saglietti, Davide Straziota
